editorial_note: Scheduled cloud handoff-only run for 2026-10-08 (Thursday). No breaking real-estate or lifestyle story cleared the full primary-record + two-independent-origin + currency + image bar this run (see discovery_notes and leads_surveyed_not_selected), so the routine produced the Biggest Permits of the Week recurring data format (frontend/docs/RECURRING_DATA_FORMATS.md, format 2), due on the Thursday run. Using the most recently completed Monday-Sunday week (Sept. 28-Oct. 4, 2026), Columbus issued 28 new-structure building permits worth a combined $66,831,507, the highest weekly declared value CREN found in the eight weeks it checked back to Aug. 10, 2026. CREN grouped permits sharing a parcel number into single projects before ranking: a four-permit, 273-unit apartment cluster on one parcel in ZIP 43016 near the Dublin-Columbus line ($29.05M) and a two-permit commercial project at 1100 Harmon Ave. on the South Side, ZIP 43223 ($28.2M), together accounted for about 86% of the week's value. CREN cross-checked the Perrins Lane parcel against the Franklin County Auditor's property record, confirming it was still classified as vacant commercial land with no building value, consistent with construction not yet underway, and that it is owned by an entity called Havery Run LLC. The Franklin County Auditor's database was down for scheduled maintenance when CREN checked the Harmon Avenue parcel, and no independent news coverage naming a developer for either project was found this run; both gaps are disclosed in the article rather than filled with an unverified guess. No lifestyle story was independently verified to the two-origin bar this run (persistent gap, carried from prior weeks). This receipt records the editorial outcome only; it is never publication authority. No import, image preparation, email delivery, or publication is claimed, and no git commit is treated as publication or downstream-import success.

story_facts_verified.weekly_total: City of Columbus Building Permits open data (ArcGIS feature service, CC0 1.0), queried October 8, 2026: 28 new-structure permits (GENERAL_TYPE ending 'New Structure') issued Sept. 28-Oct. 4, 2026 (ISSUED_DT >= 2026-09-28 and < 2026-10-05), total declared value $66,831,507. Compared against the same query for each of the seven prior weeks back to Aug. 10, 2026 (Aug10-17 $25,440,372/18 permits; Aug17-24 $16,594,441/38; Aug24-31 $10,307,874/26; Aug31-Sep7 $33,738,340/10; Sep7-14 $37,042,261/14; Sep14-21 $8,164,645/19; Sep21-28 $48,457,210/38): the Sept. 28-Oct. 4 week is the highest total of the eight.
story_facts_verified.top_projects: After grouping permits sharing a B1_PARCEL_NBR into projects: parcel 010296461 (5151 Perrins Ln. 119u/$12.5M, 5211 Perrins Ln. Unit 1101 118u/$11.5M, 5294 Haggerston Blvd. 36u/$4.1M, 5180 Riggins Run 0u/$950,000; ZIP 43016) totals $29,050,000 and 273 units, the week's largest project by combined value. Parcel 010351934 (1100 Harmon Ave. $27,000,000 and 1100 Harmon Ave. Unit Mech $1,200,000; ZIP 43223) totals $28,200,000, the single largest permit of the week. Three further standalone permits round out the top five: 1250 Briarmeadow Dr. (ZIP 43235, $1,011,668, 1 unit), 6250 Westbourne Ave. (ZIP 43035, $1,000,000, commercial), and 504 W. 1st Ave. (ZIP 43201, $650,000, 1 unit).
story_facts_verified.property_record_check: Franklin County Auditor Datalet record for parcel 010-296461-00 (pin 01029646100, jurisdiction 025), accessed October 8, 2026: owner of record Havery Run LLC, property class '400 - COMMERCIAL VACANT LAND', 9.829 acres, $0 improvement value -- confirms the site had not begun construction as of the auditor's current record. The same Auditor system returned 'System is currently unavailable due to maintenance' for parcel 010-351934-00 (the Harmon Avenue site) when checked the same day, so CREN could not confirm that parcel's owner this run.
story_facts_verified.original_contributions: Parcel-level grouping of the week's 28 raw permits into projects (surfacing the four-permit Perrins Lane cluster and the two-permit Harmon Avenue project, neither visible from an address-only read of the feed); an eight-week declared-value comparison (Aug. 10-Oct. 4, 2026) establishing this week as the period's highest; and a Franklin County Auditor cross-check of the week's largest project's parcel, confirming pre-construction status and ownership where the city feed alone does not show either.
story_facts_verified.limitations_stated: Declared value is the applicant's own construction-cost estimate, not an appraisal or sale price; a permit is legal permission to build, not proof construction has started; the Auditor record for the Harmon Avenue parcel could not be checked due to a system maintenance outage; no independent news coverage naming a developer for either top project was found this run.
